extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators and applicants preparing NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: A news/update page summarizing recent NIH policy, process, and resource announcements relevant to preparing and submitting NIH grant applications (models selection, application formats, data management, peer review changes, and reproducibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select models that are most appropriate for the research question (NAMs guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance our understanding of human health and disease. Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scientifically sound models that maximize human relevance and translational potential, but prioritize the model best matched to the specific research question rather than adopting a model solely because it is a promoted or new approach methodology (NAM).

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects application format and key features
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the PF5 overview to understand the required application format and be aware that, after peer review and before JIT, applications may be split into linked awards — plan submissions and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans using the 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for applicable submissions, use the 2026 Pilot format and include the simplified set of required elements specified in that format; consult the new resource for exact element requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research
rubrics_metrics.description: The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design applications and study plans to incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations where appropriate; review NIH’s Replication and Reproducibility Initiative and related guidance to identify opportunities to strengthen rigor and reliability in proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the 'Competitive But Not Discussed' (CBND) review designation and cutoff effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that, under the emergency modifications implemented after the lapse in appropriations, applications in the middle third may receive a CBND designation and not be discussed in full study section review even if competitive; plan for potential outcomes and consider resubmission strategies if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate effects of centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR). Centralization is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of the consolidation of peer review services and consider possible changes in review processes or timelines resulting from centralization; consult CSR guidance/resources for updates on how consolidation may affect review and application handling.
